newsitem.title: GERMANY: German NATO general denies reported Bosnia remarks.
newsitem.headline: German NATO general denies reported Bosnia remarks.

text.p: NATO general Dieter Stoeckmann denied media reports that he had said peacekeepers should stay on in Bosnia for another two or three years after their present mandate runs out in December.

A spokesman representing Stoeckmann, the chief of staff of NATO's Central European Allied Land Forces, also said late on Saturday that the general had no intention of anticipating decisions that were the responsibility of politicians.
"The report is wrong and the general has confirmed he did not say that. We can confirm he did not say the mission should last two to three more years," the spokesman said.
"There is no doubt that this decision is a matter for the politicians," he added on behalf of the general.
Bonn's defence ministry had rapped the general, saying his remarks reported in the German media were unauthorised and incorrect and that he had no right to say how long troops should stay in Bosnia.
About 50,000 troops from 34 countries under American leadership are deployed in Bosnia to help implement the Dayton peace accord which ended 43 months of war last December.

NATO-led IFOR's mandate runs out in December, but plans are already under way to begin pulling out after Bosnian elections. It is still not certain whether some form of security force will remain after the official IFOR pull-out.

Germany's Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Defence Minister Volker Ruehe have said some kind of security force was needed until military equilibrium between the former warring parties had been established and such a force would probably include German troops.
Most other NATO countries have said little and Washington has refused to comment until after U.S. elections on November 5.
